All use cases ↗

Confirm the account identity

Similar company names, parent companies, and regional sites can lead research in the wrong direction. Begin with the approved account name, domain, location if relevant, and the people involved in the upcoming conversation. Ask Nema to call out any identity conflict before it builds the brief.

Include the date of the meeting and the reason for the research. A renewal discussion needs different context from a first discovery call.

Combine public and internal context

Supply official company pages, public announcements, and other allowed sources. Add only the internal notes the Slack audience may access. Nema can place public facts and account history in separate sections, each with its source or record date.

This structure makes age visible. A strategic priority described two years ago may still matter, but the brief should not present it as current without newer support. An internal note from an earlier opportunity should retain its author and date.

Label hypotheses as hypotheses

Research often suggests questions rather than answers. A hiring page may indicate investment in a function, but it does not prove a budget or buying project. Ask Nema to keep such interpretations in a hypothesis section and propose a respectful question the representative can ask.

The same rule applies to inferred organizational problems, competitor use, and intent. A useful brief helps the account executive enter the conversation informed without pretending to know what the buyer has not said.

Prepare for a real conversation

Keep the output short enough to use. Lead with the meeting purpose, known participants, recent account history, current public developments, and unresolved questions. Include links so the representative can inspect any detail that changes their approach.

Review the brief in the deal's Slack thread. The account owner can remove irrelevant material, correct an old note, and choose which questions belong in the meeting. Nema updates the brief around that decision.

Start with one active account

Choose an account with clean identity information and an upcoming meeting. Supply a few approved sources and the relevant notes. Check every statement and remove anything the meeting participants do not need. This first run also tests whether the chosen Slack channel has the right audience.

Questions from sales teams

Can Nema research private company information?

It can use public material and connected sources the requester may access. It should not present private details that were not supplied or authorized.

How current are public facts?

The brief should include links and checked dates. The account executive can then decide whether an older source remains useful.

Is this the same as meeting preparation?

Account research builds a reusable view of the company and history. Meeting preparation narrows that context to a specific event, participants, agenda, and decision.
